paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of this whole chapter: the LORD is in charge, and we're not. Solomon opens with the king's heart as "a waterway in the hand of the LORD," and he closes with "victory is of the LORD" (Proverbs 21:1, 31). Even the most powerful man in the land is a stream in God's hand, and a horse, no matter how well prepared, doesn't get the final say. I've lost arguments with an oven timer, so I'm not exactly shocked.

In between, Solomon keeps pointing at the heart. "All a man's ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart" (Proverbs 21:2). That's why doing "righteousness and justice" matters more to the LORD than sacrifice (Proverbs 21:3). Pride, lying, laziness, a closed ear to the poor and a loose tongue all start inside, and the LORD sees every bit of it. Meanwhile, the one who "pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor" (Proverbs 21:21).

So here's what to carry out of my bakery today, baker. Plan carefully, work hard, guard your mouth, give without holding back, and don't trust your own sense of being right. Ask the LORD to weigh your heart, because He sees what you can't. "There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD" (Proverbs 21:30), so the safest place to stand is on His side.
